figures.title: Array insertion: make a gap
figures.description: Shift the suffix before writing the new value into the live array.
figures.keyIdea: Move the suffix right to left before writing the new value. Otherwise an unread value can be overwritten.

figures.title: Unlinking a known list node
figures.description: Bypass the middle node in both directions, then clear its links.
figures.keyIdea: Repair both neighbors, then detach the removed node. A forward link and its backward link must agree.

figures.title: Stack: last in, first out
figures.description: Push and pop share the top; the newest value leaves first.
figures.keyIdea: The top is the final live array element. Appending and removing there gives last-in, first-out order.

figures.title: Queue wrap: slots versus order
figures.description: The head moves around the buffer while FIFO order stays intact.
figures.keyIdea: At logical offset i, use (head + i) % capacity. Dequeue follows logical order, never raw slot order.

figures.title: Hash collisions: keep both keys
figures.description: Equal hash codes select one bucket; key equality still decides a match.
figures.keyIdea: A shared hash only selects a bucket. Equality still distinguishes the mappings; a collision must preserve both.

figures.title: LRU: a hit changes the order
figures.description: Promote a cache hit before deciding which entry to evict next.
figures.keyIdea: A hit changes recency. On overflow, evict the left end; the map points straight to the node to move.

figures.title: AVL rotation
figures.description: Inserting 30, 20 and 10 produces a left-heavy chain. A right rotation makes 20 the root with children 10 and 30, preserving in-order traversal and restoring height one.
figures.keyIdea: Rotate links, preserve sorted order, and restore the height balance.

figures.title: Heap: array and tree
figures.description: Bottom-up heapify turns 9,4,7,1,3,2 into the array 1,3,2,4,9,7. The matching complete binary tree labels every zero-based array slot and keeps every parent no greater than its children.
figures.keyIdea: A heap puts the minimum at its root; the array is not globally sorted.

figures.title: Trie: preserve shared prefixes
figures.description: The words car, cart and cat share a c-a prefix. Deleting car clears the r node's word marker but preserves its t child for cart and the sibling t branch for cat.
figures.keyIdea: Deleting a word clears its end marker. Keep nodes still needed by longer words.

figures.title: Union-find components
figures.description: Union operations on five indices produce components {0,1,2} and {3,4}. Parent arrows point toward roots 0 and 3, whose component sizes are three and two. Finding index 2 follows its link to root 0.
figures.keyIdea: Connectivity is a partition: five indices form two disjoint components.

figures.title: Fenwick prefix blocks
figures.description: For values 2,-1,4,3, one-based Fenwick slots cover [0,1), [0,2), [2,3) and [0,4). The prefix ending at zero-based boundary 3 combines slots 3 and 2: 4+1=5.
figures.keyIdea: A prefix query combines disjoint blocks. The low bit gives each block's length.

figures.title: Segment minimum
figures.description: An interval tree over 8,3,7,5 answers the minimum on [1,4) by combining leaf [1,2) with node [2,4). Replacing index 1 with 9 repairs its ancestors and changes the query answer from 3 to 5. Leaves use power-of-two padding with MAX_VALUE when needed.
figures.keyIdea: Each node covers an adjacent interval. A point set repairs one path to the root.

figures.title: Binary search: lower bound
figures.description: Half-open ranges find the first target among duplicate values.
figures.keyIdea: Keep the first possible index inside [low, high]. A value at least the target moves high left, so duplicates cannot hide the first match.

figures.title: Merge sort: split and combine
figures.description: Split into singletons, then merge sorted children bottom up.
figures.keyIdea: Each parent merges two sorted children. A level costs O(n) work, and there are O(log n) levels: O(n log n) overall.

figures.title: Quicksort: three-way partition
figures.description: Gather duplicate pivot values into one finished equal region.
figures.keyIdea: Only the smaller and greater regions recurse. Equal keys already belong together, so the equal region needs no further sorting.

figures.title: Coin change: build an optimum
figures.description: Compare every final coin; the largest-first greedy choice loses.
figures.keyIdea: best[a] is optimal for exactly amount a. Each candidate adds one coin to a solved, strictly smaller amount.

figures.title: 0/1 knapsack: sweep backward
figures.description: Sweep capacities backward so an item cannot reuse itself.
figures.keyIdea: Descending capacity keeps the current item out of its own predecessor states. Each item is used at most once.

figures.title: KMP: keep the overlap
figures.description: Prefix fallback retains the overlap between two pattern matches.
figures.keyIdea: After a match, retain the longest matched suffix that is also a pattern prefix. This preserves overlapping matches without rescanning text.

figures.title: N-queens: reject and undo
figures.description: Trace failed placements before reaching the first valid board.
figures.keyIdea: Place one queen per row. Reject used columns or diagonals; undo an unsuccessful choice before trying another.

figures.title: Greedy: finish first
figures.description: Choose earliest finishing intervals; touching endpoints remain compatible.
figures.keyIdea: The earliest finishing compatible activity leaves at least as much time for everything that follows. This maximizes the count, not total duration.

figures.title: Bubble sort: adjacent swaps
figures.description: Swap neighboring values; each pass settles a maximum on the right.
figures.keyIdea: Each adjacent comparison moves the larger value right. After a pass, the unsorted range's maximum is fixed at its end; a swap-free pass stops.

figures.title: BFS: discovered vs processed
figures.description: Follow the queue separately from discovery; isolate unreachable vertex 5.
figures.keyIdea: Discovery happens on enqueue, before processing; isolated vertices stay unreachable.

figures.title: Dijkstra: distance and path
figures.description: Compare weighted routes from source 0 and distinguish unreachable vertex 4.
figures.keyIdea: Choose the cheapest weighted path; absence is separate from every numeric distance.

figures.title: Negative edge or cycle?
figures.description: A negative edge yields -3; an added cycle makes targets 1 and 2 unbounded.
figures.keyIdea: A negative edge can be safe; this API rejects any reachable negative cycle.

figures.title: SCCs and bridges differ
figures.description: Directed return paths form SCCs; undirected essential edges are bridges.
figures.keyIdea: SCCs test directed mutual reachability; bridges test an undirected edge's necessity.

figures.title: Compare growth, not timings
figures.description: Five illustrative functions share a value of one at input size one. A logarithmic work axis shows logarithmic, linear, n log n, quadratic and exponential growth without implying benchmark timings.
figures.keyIdea: Theoretical normalized work; constants, machines and measured runtime are outside this comparison.

traces.description: Shrink a half-open interval while keeping the first possible match.
traces.keyIdea: A matching midpoint is a candidate, so retain it by moving high.

traces.keyIdea: Mark on enqueue, so shared neighbors cannot schedule the same vertex twice.

frames.summary: Mark vertex 0 discovered before enqueueing it. No vertex enters the queue twice.

traces.title: Dijkstra: improve, then settle
traces.description: Track tentative distances, relax directed weighted edges, and discard stale heap entries.
traces.keyIdea: Choose the smallest tentative distance; a FIFO queue cannot replace this priority rule.

frames.title: Initialize tentative distances
frames.explanation: Distance to source 0 is zero. Other distances are not yet known. Heap rows show pending candidates in priority order, not physical heap storage.
frames.summary: Distance to source 0 is zero. Other distances are not yet known. Heap rows show pending candidates in priority order, not physical heap storage.

frames.title: Settle vertex 0 at distance 0
frames.explanation: This is the smallest pending distance. Nonnegative edges ensure no later route can improve this settled value.
frames.summary: This is the smallest pending distance. Nonnegative edges ensure no later route can improve this settled value.

frames.title: Relax 0 → 1
frames.explanation: 0 + edge weight 5 = 5, improving unknown. Record parent 0 and push candidate 1:5.
frames.summary: 0 + edge weight 5 = 5, improving unknown. Record parent 0 and push candidate 1:5.

frames.title: Relax 0 → 2
